newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab gunmen kill two Israelis, wound five.
newsitem.headline: Arab gunmen kill two Israelis, wound five.

text.p: Arab gunmen shot dead a twelve-year-old Israeli boy and his mother in a drive-by shooting near the PLO-ruled West Bank town of Ramallah on Wednesday, Israeli security sources and hospital officials said.

Five others -- all from the same family who security sources said were Jewish settlers -- were wounded after the attack by Arab gunmen in a car with number plates issued to Palestinians in the West Bank. The army said the car fled towards Ramallah.

Israeli Major General Uzi Dayan, commander of areas including the West Bank, told Israel television a car fitting the description of the attackers' car had gone up in flames at a garbage dump in Ramallah and that Israeli forces had entered to investigate. He later said entry was coordinated with the PLO.
Jibril Rajoub, head of security in Palestinian-ruled areas of the West Bank, told Reuters:
"The Israeli side applied...for permission to enter Ramallah to look at the car. We have no objections. They will be escorted by Palestinian police."
After the attack Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority in charge of self-rule enclaves "that Israel would not let the incident pass quietly".
"The prime minister adds that the Palestinian Authority cannot give cover to terrorists and murderers of children," the statement issued by Netanyahu's office said.
It said Netanyahu and Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai had discussed the incident "and the two decided to take immediate steps which the defence minister will announce."
Netanyahu's office said he had sent "a sharp message" to Arafat. It did not reveal the contents of the message.

Witnesses said the Israelis' blue Volkswagon station wagon was riddled with bullet holes. It was at a stop sign near Beit El Jewish settlement just outside of Ramallah about 25 km (15 miles) north of Jerusalem on a road connecting Beit El to another Jewish settlement, Talmon.

Security sources said there were three Arab gunmen who shot at the Israeli family's car from a passing Subaru. Dayan told Israel Radio the father of the family, lightly wounded in the attack, had described the car.

An Israeli police spokesman said the 12-year-old boy died shortly after the attack. A spokesman for Jerusalem's Hadassah Ein Kerem hospital confirmed to Reuters that the mother of the boy later died of her wounds.
He said three children aged about four to 10 years old had also been wounded. The army said one of the wounded was in moderate condition and the others had been lightly hurt.
The army said it imposed a closure on Ramallah and its forces were searching for the attackers.

Defence Minister Mordechai's office issued a statement saying he "ordered security forces this evening to act with all the force necessary in order to find and capture the unit of murderers...(he) asked the Palestinian Authority to find the murderers and to extradite them if they are in the area of the jurisdiction of the Palestinian Authority."

Jewish settler spokesman Aharon Domb demanded the army initiate "hot pursuit", a search for wanted persons, in the self-rule enclave telling Israel Radio it was "the drill" for guerrillas to escape to self-rule areas. He later said Mordechai and army brass were meeting with settlers at Beit El.
The issue of "hot pursuit" has snagged talks PLO-Israel on a Israeli handover of most of the West Bank town of Hebron.

Ramallah with five other West Bank towns was handed to the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) at the end of 1995 under a deal signed more than a year ago between the PLO and Israel's previous government. Hebron was to have been handed over in March but this was delayed after Moslem militant attacks in Israel.
An Israeli was killed in a similar drive-by shooting near Beit El in May. The last such attack occurred in Israel near the border with the West Bank in July when Arab gunmen killed two Israelis.
